task: Build a molecule-level literature dataset of experimental phototoxicity, skin irritation, corrosion, and local tissue-damage evidence. Include 3T3 NRU phototoxicity, light-dependent ROS or cytotoxicity, UV-dependent responses, reconstructed skin irritation or corrosion assays, keratinocyte damage, inflammatory responses, and local tissue injury.
task_instantiation:
Extract molecule- or compound-class-level experimental evidence that a test substance causes, does not cause, or protects against phototoxicity/photosensitivity, light-dependent ROS or cytotoxicity, UV-dependent cutaneous damage, skin irritation, skin corrosion, keratinocyte damage, local inflammatory responses, or local tissue injury. Create one record for each substance × assay/test system × materially distinct exposure condition × endpoint/result; split dose levels, light conditions, models, or endpoints when they have separate results, but keep multiple time points or related readouts from the same condition in one record. Include human, animal, reconstructed-tissue, ex vivo, and cell-based experiments, including explicit clinical incidence or confirmed challenge/rechallenge evidence. Include both positive and negative results and protective effects only when the substance is experimentally linked to one of the target local-damage endpoints. Quantitative values from prose or clearly identified tables/figures are valid; qualitative author conclusions are also valid. Use the listed molecule or class entity as the top-level `global_identifier`; do not emit a record when no tested substance/class can be attributed.

Exclude systemic acute toxicity (for example oral LD50), sensitization/allergic contact dermatitis assays unless a direct irritant or light-dependent tissue reaction is separately reported, generic descriptions of assay principles/protocols, assay validation statistics, irradiation parameters without a substance-specific outcome, tested concentration without a result, photostability/photoisomerization alone, pigmentation or immunosuppression without damage/inflammation, and light-dependent antimicrobial/antiviral activity unless mammalian skin/tissue/cell damage is also measured. Do not treat generic UV erythema in untreated subjects as molecule evidence. Do not infer phototoxicity merely from light absorption, ROS mechanism, increased cytotoxicity, a PIF/MPE number, or a comparison; assign `result_label` from the authors' explicit interpretation or an explicitly stated assay classification. If no overall label is stated, use `result_label` = `not_classified` and report the measured effect faithfully. Comparative claims without an absolute result are eligible only if they directly establish a target effect for the indexed substance; describe the comparator in `extra_details` and do not invent values.

Map the main endpoint to `evidence_endpoint`, the model level to `evidence_system`, and the named assay/model to `assay_method`. Put dose/concentration, vehicle/formulation, route/application, species/cell/tissue, duration, sample size, and observation time in `experimental_conditions`; put wavelength/source, irradiance/fluence, exposure duration, and light-versus-dark design in `light_conditions`. Report numeric outcomes, incidence, scores, PIF/MPE, ROS/cytotoxicity changes, or lesion descriptions in `observed_effect`. Assume ordinary assay or clinical conditions when unspecified. Put only exceptional conditions that materially limit generalization—such as preselected previously reactive subjects, diseased/damaged tissue, unusual barrier disruption, genetic manipulation, or required co-treatment—in `qualifying_conditions`; otherwise set it to null. Routine dose, species, cell line, tissue, light dose, and time point are not qualifying conditions.

schema_spec.name: evidence_endpoint
schema_spec.description: Primary local-damage endpoint measured or explicitly concluded for this substance and condition.

schema_spec.name: evidence_system
schema_spec.description: Highest-level experimental or clinical test system in which the substance-specific result was obtained.

schema_spec.name: assay_method
schema_spec.description: Named assay, challenge, measurement method, or study design, such as 3T3 NRU PT, reconstructed epidermis irritation test, patch test, photopatch/rechallenge, ROS assay, or histology.

schema_spec.name: result_label
schema_spec.description: Overall interpretation for the target endpoint: positive = harmful effect/classification present; negative = absent; protective = reduced/prevented target damage; mixed_or_inconclusive = conflicting or explicitly equivocal; not_classified = measurements are reported but no overall interpretation is stated. Do not infer classification from thresholds unless the paper explicitly applies them.

schema_spec.name: observed_effect
schema_spec.description: Reported qualitative or quantitative result, including incidence/counts, score, effect size, concentration-response, PIF/MPE, ROS/cytotoxicity change, or tissue lesion; preserve units and comparator/reference.

schema_spec.name: experimental_conditions
schema_spec.description: Routine non-light conditions: dose/concentration, formulation/vehicle, route or application, species/cell/tissue, exposure and observation times, replicate or subject count, and relevant controls.

schema_spec.name: light_conditions
schema_spec.description: Light context when relevant: UVA/UVB/visible source or wavelength, irradiance/fluence, exposure duration/timing, and light-versus-dark comparison. Null for non-photochemical irritation/corrosion/injury evidence.

schema_spec.name: qualifying_conditions
schema_spec.description: Exceptional context materially limiting generalization, such as preselected reactive subjects, diseased or barrier-disrupted tissue, genetic manipulation, or required co-treatment. Null for standard or unspecified conditions; do not place routine assay parameters here.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
